metadata.title: Tee Higgins - Will be limited Wednesday
metadata.description: Higgins (adductor) will be limited in practice Wednesday, Ben Baby of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: With Higgins having been labeled day-to-day earlier in the week, his return to practice in any capacity is a positive step for his Week 5 availability against the Dolphins. The Bengals are going to need Higgins if Ja'Marr Chase is unable to clear concussion protocol. Dohnte Meyers and Mike Gesicki would be next in line for targets, and both are sensible fantasy pickups this week.

metadata.title: Tee Higgins (adductor) to be limited in practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Tee Higgins will be limited in practice on Wednesday.
metadata.analysis: It is a good sign to start the week for Higgins. His status will need to continue to be monitored the next couple of days.

metadata.title: Tee Higgins (adductor) listed day-to-day
metadata.description: Tee Higgins (adductor) was labeled day-to-day by Bengals head coach Zac Taylor on Monday.
metadata.analysis: Higgins had a huge game Sunday after fellow Cincy receiver Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) was knocked out of the loss to the Jaguars early. Higgins was clearly dealing with an injury of his own late in the game, however. It was later revealed to be an adductor issue, but it appears the injury is considered mild. Higgins should be monitored at practice this week.

metadata.title: Tee Higgins - Deemed day-to-day
metadata.description: Higgins (adductor), per head coach Zac Taylor, is considered day-to-day, Ben Baby of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: Higgins emerged from Sunday's loss to the Jaguars with an adductor issue, but he appears to have avoided any sort of serious setback. More will be know about Higgins' status by Wednesday at the latest, when the Bengals provide an official update on the health of Higgins -- as well as fellow wideout Ja'Marr Chase (concussion).

metadata.title: Tee Higgins Day-to-Day With Adductor Injury
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins (adductor) is considered day-to-day after leaving Sunday's loss to Jacksonville late in the fourth quarter. Head coach Zac Taylor told Paul Dehner on Monday that Higgins has not been ruled out for Week 5 and that the team will see where he is as the week goes on. Higgins tried to return for one play after the injury but could not continue. Before leaving, he had already put together his best game of the season, catching 11 passes for 157 yards on 16 targets. He now has 25 receptions for 401 yards and one touchdown through four games. Cincinnati visits Miami on Sunday before its Week 6 bye, so the next few practices should give a much better indication of whether Higgins can avoid missing time.

metadata.title: Tee Higgins suffers adductor injury Sunday
metadata.description: Bengals WR Tee Higgins suffered an adductor injury late in Sunday's loss to Jacksonville.
metadata.analysis: Higgins had an excellent day against Jacksonville, but suffered the injury late and was unable to go back into the game. Fantasy managers will want to monitor his status ahead of a Week 5 matchup with Miami.

metadata.title: Tee Higgins - Suffers adductor injury in Week 4
metadata.description: Higgins sustained an adductor issue during Sunday's 22-17 loss to the Jaguars, Ben Baby of ESPN.com reports.
metadata.analysis: The Bengals played most of Week 4 without top WR Ja'Marr Chase, who suffered a concussion in the first half. The situation allowed Higgins to rack up a whopping 11-157-0 line on 16 targets, but he also picked up a health concern himself. With Colbie Young (knee) inactive Sunday and Andrei Iosivas (thumb) on IR for at least two more contests, the Bengals currently are down to just two healthy wide receivers on the active roster (Dohnte Meyers and Mitchell Tinsley).

metadata.title: Tee Higgins Dealing With Abductor Injury
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins is dealing with an abductor injury, head coach Zac Taylor said after Sunday's 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, according to Charlie Clifford. Higgins was hurt after making a 19-yard catch late in the fourth quarter and needed attention from the training staff. He missed the next play but returned later in the drive, catching a pass on his first snap back. Higgins finished with 11 receptions for 157 yards, easily his best receiving total through four games. Taylor did not provide a timetable or any additional details on the injury immediately after the game.

metadata.title: Tee Higgins Could Go Off Against Jaguars
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins is coming off his best performance of the season in last week's loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers. Higgins racked up six catches for 90 yards and a touchdown in the 27-30 loss in Week 3. The Bengals WR2 can easily finish any week as a fantasy WR1 given the potency of this offense. Higgins will have the opportunity to go off again this week against the Jacksonville Jaguars. The Jaguars defense has been strong to start the year, but the duo of Ja'Marr Chase and Higgins is arguably the best one-two punch at wide receiver in the league. Higgins could also be heavily involved because of the strength of the Jaguars offense. Through the first three weeks, the Jacksonville offense has actually scored more points than the Bengals, so Cincinnati could be chasing points in this game. Higgins is ranked WR14 in our RotoBaller Week 4 PPR rankings, making him a borderline WR1/strong WR2 in this matchup. Fantasy managers should be excited about having a wideout in what should be a high-scoring game.

metadata.title: Tee Higgins finds the end zone in Week 3 loss
metadata.description: Tee Higgins caught 6-of-7 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in a 30-27 loss to the Steelers.
metadata.analysis: Higgins was just behind Ja'Marr Chase in targets, receptions, and receiving yards in the loss Sunday. He found the end zone for the first time this season on an impressive 28-yard reception prior to halftime. Higgins and the Bengals will welcome the Jaguars to town in Week 4.

metadata.title: Tee Higgins Strikes for His First Touchdown of the Season in Week 3
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins caught six of seven targets for 90 yards and one touchdown during Sunday's Week 3 contest against the Pittsburgh Steelers. In addition to finding the end zone for the first time this year, Higgins' six catches represented a new season-high mark. The 27-year-old has repeatedly proven that he can co-exist with Ja'Marr Chase in fantasy football, and he remains a must-start WR2 going forward. As long as quarterback Joe Burrow is healthy, Higgins is a safe bet to get peppered with targets while making difficult catches and offering some touchdown upside. With that said, he's currently on pace for just six touchdowns this year, which is a significant step back from his 10 in 2024 and his 11 in 2025. Perhaps he can improve on that pace with another big game and visit to the end zone in a potential Week 4 shootout against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

metadata.title: Tee Higgins - Efficient in Week 3 loss
metadata.description: Higgins brought in six of seven targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals' 30-27 loss to the Steelers on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Higgins and Ja'Marr Chase turned in signature performances in the high-scoring loss, and the former finished as the runner-up in receptions, receiving yards and targets on the day to his talented teammate. Higgins' first score of the season came on a 28-yard grab late in the first half, knotting the score at 17-17 going into halftime. Through three games, Higgins is on pace for a potential third career 1,000-yard season, as he's quickly amassed a 14-244-1 line on 23 targets.

metadata.title: Tee Higgins Could Smash On The Road In Pittsburgh
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins will face the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 3. The Bengals WR2 was the most targeted pass catcher in last week's 20-6 victory over the Houston Texans. Despite not scoring a touchdown, Higgins was able to lead the Bengals in receiving yards in Week 2. The 27-year-old will try to replicate that performance this week on the road at Pittsburgh. The Steelers have been a good pass defense to start the 2026 season, but Cincinnati's passing attack is much better than most. Higgins has historically been a great touchdown-scoring receiver and he hasn't found pay dirt this year, so the trips to the end zone could start this Sunday. Higgins is ranked WR18 in our RotoBaller Week 3 PPR rankings, making him a strong WR2 this week. Fantasy managers should be encouraged by the volume of opportunities Higgins has had so far and excited for what's to come in this week's matchup.

metadata.title: Tee Higgins racks up 95 yards Sunday
metadata.description: Tee Higgins caught 5-of-10 targets for 95 yards in the Bengals 20-6 win over the Texans on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Higgins recorded several big catch and runs in the first half against a strong Texans defense. He remains an upside WR2 heading into next week against the Steelers.

metadata.title: Tee Higgins - Team-high yardage in Week 2 win
metadata.description: Higgins secured five of 10 targets for 95 yards in the Bengals' 20-6 win over the Texans on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Higgins' receiving yardage and target totals paced the Bengals on the afternoon, and he finished second only to Ja'Marr Chase in receiving yards. The talented wide receiver duo accounted for 12 of Joe Burrow's 20 completions against a tough Texans defense, and Higgins now is averaging an elite 19.3 yards per reception on his first eight catches of the 2026 season. The veteran speedster will aim to continue thriving downfield in a Week 3 road matchup against the Steelers next Sunday.

metadata.title: Tee Higgins Leads Bengals Pass-Catchers In Houston
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins caught five passes for 95 yards in the 20-6 win over the Houston Texans on the road. Higgins paced the team in both receiving yards and targets in a big win over a strong Texans defense. While fellow wideout Ja'Marr Chase found the end zone twice, Higgins displayed his ability to keep pace as a top target on this team. Higgins will look to continue being effective next week on the road against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Higgins is in for another tough defensive matchup in Week 3, but he was just able to produce against the Texans defense so fantasy managers should feel confident in starting him. Higgins should be viewed as one of the strongest WR2 options with WR1 upside any given week.

metadata.title: Tee Higgins Poised For A Big Game In Week 2
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins will take on the Houston Texans on the road this Sunday. Higgins had a mediocre performance against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last week, catching three passes for 59 yards. Higgins connected with quarterback Joe Burrow a few times, notably on a 29-yard reception, but couldn't find the end zone, finishing with just 8.9 points in PPR formats. While the performance was not a complete dud, it was not the type of game that fantasy managers expect from Higgins in a high-scoring game. In Higgins' career, he's been completely healthy for 76 games and in that span he's scored 45 touchdowns. That's good for 0.59 touchdowns per game when healthy, for context, future Hall of Fame WR Mike Evans has a career rate of 0.61 touchdowns per game. Higgins is among the best receivers in the league at finding pay dirt and he has a high chance to do so this Sunday in a game against the Texans with an over/under set at 46.5 points. The Texans just allowed the Bills to score 36 points against them in Week 1, so the Bengals should be able to score on them as well. Higgins is ranked WR22 in our RotoBaller Week 2 PPR rankings, placing him firmly in the WR2 discussion. Fantasy managers should expect a much better performance from Higgins in Week 2.

metadata.title: Tee Higgins totals 59 yards Sunday
metadata.description: Tee Higgins caught 3-of-6 targets for 59 yards in the Bengals 33-27 win over the Buccaneers.
metadata.analysis: It could have been worse. You could have Ja'Marr Chase catching two passes for 12 yards. It wasn't the most inspiring start to the season for Higgins, but he still had a couple of big catches. He'll remain an upside WR2 heading into Week 2 against the Texans.

metadata.title: Tee Higgins - Efficient with three catches
metadata.description: Higgins brought in three of six targets for 59 yards in the Bengals' 33-27 win over the Buccaneers on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Higgins tied for second in receptions and targets while also serving as the runner-up in receiving yards for the Bengals on an afternoon in which Joe Burrow spread the ball around to nine different targets. The veteran wideout also had a team-high 29-yard reception on one of his three grabs, while his final one of the day went for 18 yards for a key first down on the Bengals' game-sealing drive. Much more productive days are surely in store for Cincinnati's air attack, and a Week 2 road matchup against the Texans next Sunday doesn't seem as daunting after Houston's defense was repeatedly victimized by the Bills in Week 1.

metadata.title: Tee Higgins Leads Receiver Room In Week 1 Win
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins caught three passes for 59 yards in the 33-27 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 1. Higgins was able to lead the wide receiver room in receptions and yards with a down game from fellow WR Ja'Marr Chase, who only caught two passes for 12 yards. Higgins and the rest of the Bengals offense were the beneficiaries of an outstanding performance by the Cincinnati defense. With the Bengals defense forcing four turnovers and coming away with a score, the offense found themselves in advantageous situations often. Higgins and the rest of the offense will likely be more relied upon in next week's matchup against the Houston Texans. The Texans are known to be one of the strongest units in the league, so fantasy points may be at a premium for the Bengals playmakers. Still, Higgins should be viewed as a strong WR2 because the ceiling for the Cincinnati offense is among the highest in the league.

metadata.title: Tee Higgins - Logs another full practice
metadata.description: Higgins (heel) will play in Sunday's game against Tampa Bay after logging full practices Wednesday through Friday.
metadata.analysis: Ja'Marr Chase (knee) also is cleared to play, giving Joe Burrow plenty of firepower for the regular-season opener. Higgins seemed to stay healthy throughout spring and summer before missing a few practices with a heel contusion last week. He should be ready for his usual role come Sunday.

metadata.title: Tee Higgins (foot) cleared for Week 1
metadata.description: Tee Higgins (foot) is cleared to play in Week 1 for the Cincinnati Bengals against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers according to Kelsey Conway.

metadata.title: Tee Higgins Removed From Injury Report, Ready For Full Workload
metadata.description: Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Tee Higgins was listed on the Week 1 injury report with a foot injury but was a full participant in all practices and has since been removed from the injury report ahead of Sunday. Higgins and the Bengals will take on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 1 of the 2026 season. Despite his quarterback missing nine games last season, Higgins still managed to finish as the WR15 in PPR formats. Higgins will have the opportunity to pick up where he left off against the Buccaneers in what should be one of the highest-scoring games of the week. The highly talented WR2 for the Bengals is a strong WR2 option for fantasy with the upside to finish as a WR1 if he and Burrow can both stay healthy. Higgins is ranked WR11 in our RotoBaller Week 1 PPR rankings, making him a low-end WR1 option in a positive offensive environment. Fantasy managers should start Higgins with confidence this week.
